subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and should it cover only top-level navigate/open-tab requests or also redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and proxy-routed profiles?
rationale: This creates an operator-trusted browser security/config surface, so automation cannot safely choose denylist versus warnlist guarantees, bundled defaults, or traffic coverage without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design browser policy contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define hard-block versus advisory-warning semantics and the exact browser traffic classes covered before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader egress policy
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 own the work only if it explicitly covers browser navigation and browser-specific traffic classes.

options.title: Use advisory hints only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable browser denylist for now and provide only best-effort warnings for known bot-blocked sites.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define hard-block versus advisory-warning semantics and the exact browser traffic classes covered before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal is across browser SSRF config, navigation policy, and docs.
